parties.respondent_defendant: Savitri Bai and Ku. Deokibai (wife and daughter-in-law)

facts_of_case: Savitri Bai filed a suit against Halkai for maintenance, alleging desertion and cruelty. The trial court granted maintenance to Savitri Bai. Deokibai became major and married, so the trial court did not grant her maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu wife is entitled to maintenance by her husband even if she lives separately from him if he has another wife living or keeps a concubine in the same house.
legal_principles.held: Under Section 18 of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956, a Hindu wife whether married before or after the commencement of the Act is entitled to a maintenance by her husband even though she lives separately from her husband if he has another wife living, or if he keeps a concubine in the same house in which his wife is living or--habitually resides with a concubine elsewhere.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956 — Section 18
use_in: divorce cases where husband has multiple wives or concubines

legal_principles.principle: The provisions of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 override any existing laws or customs that are inconsistent with its provisions.
legal_principles.held: Section 4 gives overriding application to the provisions of the Act and in respect of any of the matters dealt with in the Act, it repeals in effect all existing laws, whether in the shape of enactments or otherwise, which are inconsistent with the Act.
use_in: cases where Hindu law is applicable and there are inconsistencies with existing laws or customs

outcome.final_order: The trial court's decision was upheld, and Halkai was not liable to pay maintenance to Savitri Bai.
